result.topic_en: Hilbert sketches an argument that the points of greatest and least 'self-distance', defined by growing geodesic circles until they touch themselves, give closed geodesics on a surface; he then discusses polyhedral models of the Steiner surface and the Boy surface obtained from a modified octahedron.

items.english: Let A be the point of greatest and B the point of least self-distance; then these two self-distances form the sought closed geodesic lines.

items.english: Which closed polyhedron corresponds to the Boy surface?

items.quote:
wenn man in einem
Oktaeder von 2 gegenüberliegenden Dreiecken nur je eines bei-
behält und das so entstehende durchlöcherte Oktaeder von
4 Dreiecken durch 3 Rechtecke ergänzt, {+dass+} man einen geschlossenen Polyeder, dieser auf

items.english: If, in an octahedron, one keeps only one of each pair of opposite triangles and completes the resulting perforated octahedron of 4 triangles with 3 rectangles, one obtains a closed polyhedron, and this can be mapped one-to-one and continuously onto the projective plane.
